description: Cross-sections of the client's pending absorbers (rendering plan R08, R08.T4.c; decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md, follow-ups 3 and 4): per species or pair and task, its 1 nm cell-mean cross-sections over 380-760 nm at its source's temperature nodes: cellMeansM2, m2 a molecule, or cellMeansM5, m5 a molecule pair, one row of 381 cells a node, the cells centred on 380, 381, ..., 760 nm, each [nm - 0.5, nm + 0.5) on vacuum wavelengths, rounded up to 3 significant figures so that each stays a bound. Reduced values from HITRAN2024, R. L. Kurucz's atomic line lists and the stated estimates, each with its citation; ExoMol's are in exomol/bounds.json. R08.T10.a bounds each channel's change by them at each body's own column.

bounds.method: Stated overtone-ladder estimate (decision-r08-t4b-t12c.md follow-up 3, ruling 3): no line list reaches 380-760 nm and no measured visible intensity was read (the papers found are closed). Each 1 nm vacuum cell's mean over 380-760 nm at 296 K: the anchor band's lines, each moved by its offset from the band's intensity-weighted centroid to the target polyad and divided by 10 for each quantum, summed in the cell [c - 0.5, c + 0.5) nm over its width in cm-1. Higher polyads, a further tenth a quantum, are not in the cells. Three CH quanta to the five-quantum band near 15600 cm-1, 10^-2: cells 638-647 nm, the largest 640 nm (8.66e-29 m2; a cell-wide window anywhere holds at most 8.83e-29).

bounds.source: Twice H- free-free's pair cross-section, T. L. John, Astron. Astrophys. 193 (1988) 189-192, Eq. 6 (absorbers/hMinus.ts), times k T
bounds.method: Bell 1980's H2- table (J. Phys. B 13, 1859, DOI 10.1088/0022-3700/13/9/016) was not obtained (no open copy; IOP's is behind a paywall). Estimated as twice H-'s free-free per atom and electron, a margin: a secondary transcription of Bell's Table 1 (PICASO's h2minus.csv, read as a check only) puts H2- at 0.53-0.93 times H-'s over 350-911 nm, so the factor is a margin of 2.1-3.8 (H2's static polarisability, 1.2 times H's, does not set it): each 1 nm vacuum cell's mean over 380-760 nm at each node, by a 10-point midpoint rule, at John's temperatures 5040/theta for theta 3.6, 2, 1 and 0.5.

bounds.source: Stated band-model estimate; no line list of N2's first or second positive system was read. Term values and vibrational constants of N2's X1Sigmag+, A3Sigmau+, B3Pig and C3Piu states as compiled by K. P. Huber and G. Herzberg, Molecular Spectra and Molecular Structure IV (1979) and A. Lofthus and P. H. Krupenie, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 6 (1977) 113, DOI 10.1063/1.555546, cross-checked against the NIST Chemistry WebBook's compilation of Huber and Herzberg (SRD 69, fetched 2026-10-11), which they match to the digits used; and against the second positive 0-0 band at 337.0 nm, the Vegard-Kaplan onset at 201 nm and the first positive 2-0 band near 775 nm
bounds.method: LTE absorption of the first positive (B3Pig <- A3Sigmau+) and second positive (C3Piu <- B3Pig) systems from the thermal populations of the A state (6.17 eV) and the B state (7.35 eV). Franck-Condon factors from Morse oscillators (1PG q(0,0..2) 0.40, 0.33, 0.17; 2PG 0.47, 0.32, 0.14); band rates A = K q nu^3, K fixed by v' = 0 radiative lifetimes taken short for an upper estimate (B 6 us, C 36 ns; C v' = 0-4, predissociated above); populations g exp(-c2 E/T) (B_X/B_L) / Q_vib(X); each band's whole strength in the cell of its origin's vacuum wavelength, so the peak cells are raised. Each 1 nm vacuum cell's mean over 380-760 nm at each node. The 1PG Delta v = 2-4 sequences dominate; the largest cell is 760 nm (the 3-1 band), tau at 1e3 km-amagat 2.5e-6 at 1800 K and 1.4e-4 at 2000 K. With two-term vibrational energies the 3-1 band's origin falls at 760.46 nm, inside the 760 nm cell (the book's omega_e y_e terms would move it to 760.61 nm); the real band is degraded to the violet, its head near 762.8 nm, so part of it lies in the cell either way, and the lumped value is an upper estimate.
